Joktan
jok'tan
n. (son of Eber and brother of Peleg; father of thirteen sons who peopled the Arabian south)
From Hebrew Yoqtan, connected with qaton, to be small or made little — the younger or lesser brother. The name sits opposite Peleg in the same verse, and the two together divide Eber's house.

Biblical Definition

Joktan is the brother of Peleg and the second son of Eber, and where Peleg's line is followed down to Abraham, Joktan's is spread out sideways. Thirteen sons are named — “And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah” (Gen 10:26), on through Ophir and Havilah and Jobab (Gen 10:29) — and their settlement is fixed: “And their dwelling was from Mesha, as thou goest unto Sephar a mount of the east” (Gen 10:30). This is the southern Arabian world, the country of the spice roads and of Ophir's gold, and it is Shemite, not Japhethite. Eber's two sons are the fork in the Shemite road. One branch becomes the Hebrews and carries the covenant; the other becomes the peoples of the Arabian peninsula, listed with the same care and given no promise. The Chronicler preserves the whole list unaltered for the returned exiles (1Ch 1:20), a people with every reason to trim the record to their own line and no inclination to do it. That restraint is a mark of Scripture's honesty. The line God did not choose is written down in full, in order, with its territory named, because these men are His creatures too and the record is a record.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Joktan; in sacred history he is the son of Eber and brother of Peleg, whose thirteen sons peopled southern Arabia.

expand to see more

JOKTAN, n. The second son of Eber, and brother of Peleg.

He begat thirteen sons, among whom were Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab.

Their dwelling was from Mesha unto Sephar, a mount of the east.

These are reckoned among the Shemites, and are supposed to have peopled the south of Arabia.

The whole list is repeated in the first book of Chronicles without variation.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:26 — "And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,"

Gen 10:29 — "And Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab: all these were the sons of Joktan."

Gen 10:30 — "And their dwelling was from Mesha, as thou goest unto Sephar a mount of the east."

1Ch 1:20 — "And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,"

Modern Corruption

Election is misread as favouritism when Scripture follows one brother and not the other; and the Arabian branch is treated as a mere aside rather than as nations God will yet call.

expand to see more

Two brothers, one father, and the narrative follows only one of them — the offence readers take at that is the offence Paul anticipated when he wrote about Jacob and Esau. The charge is that God plays favourites. The answer Scripture gives is not that the choice was earned but that the choice was free and just: “he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy” (Rom 9:15). Joktan is not condemned by being unfollowed. His house is named at length, his territory recorded, his sons preserved through the exile. What the covenant line receives is not better treatment than justice; it is mercy, and mercy that is owed is not mercy at all.

The second misreading treats the Joktanite peoples as a closed parenthesis — genealogical furniture with no future. Scripture does not leave them there. Ophir's gold comes to Solomon's temple; Sheba's queen comes to hear his wisdom and goes home confessing the LORD; and the prophets keep the Arabian south in view to the end, with Isaiah promising that the dromedaries of Midian and the flocks of Kedar shall come up with acceptance on God's altar (Isa 60:6-7). The line not chosen at Genesis 10 is not the line refused for ever. The Gentiles named in the table are the Gentiles the gospel is sent to, and the day comes when they “shall shew forth the praises of the LORD”.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yoqtan (H3355), Joktan; qaton (H6996), small, little, younger; 'Eber (H5677), Eber; moshab (H4186), dwelling, habitation; Ophir (H211), Ophir.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yoqtan (H3355) — Joktan; the second son of Eber, brother of Peleg.

Hebrew qaton (H6996) — to be small, little, younger; the root commonly connected with the name.

Hebrew 'Eber (H5677) — Eber; their father, from whose name the word Hebrew is drawn.

Hebrew moshab (H4186) — dwelling, seat, habitation; the word fixing their territory in Gen 10:30.

Hebrew 'Ophir (H211) — Ophir; a son of Joktan, and afterward the byword for fine gold.

Usage

"“All these were the sons of Joktan” — thirteen names and no promise, written down anyway."

"“From Mesha, as thou goest unto Sephar” — the record gives even the unchosen a map."

"The brother the story does not follow is still the brother the record keeps."
